newsitem.title: MAURITIUS: American companies seek business in Mauritius.
newsitem.headline: American companies seek business in Mauritius.

text.p: A delegation from 10 U.S. companies spent a week exploring business opportunities in the Indian Ocean island of Mauritius, the U.S. ambassador said on Friday.
The firms were eyeing transportation, telecommunications, energy, manufacturing, infrastructure, distribution and offshore sectors, Harold Geisel told reporters at the end of the one-week tour.

The firms were Raytheon International, General Electric, Bechtel, South Western Bell, Motorola, Dow Chemicals, National Airways Corporation, Qualcomm International, Hughes Network Systems International and Granger Telecom.

"These firms are world leaders in industry and technology. I think it shows that Mauritians are looking towards the future. People here are looking for the best products at the best prices," the U.S ambassador told reporters.
Some delegation members said the visit opened new prospects.

"We have seen dynamic and pragmatic people both in the private sector and in government," said Joachim Schoch, managing director of Dow Chemicals. "Mauritius is not a place full of natural resources but rather a trading, technology, distribution place."
Millard Arnold, U.S embassy minister counselor for commercial affairs for southern Africa, said it was premature to predict business plans.
"But one businessman in the trade delegation said to me if things work out correctly, the U.S. can do business with Mauritius worth $1 billion," Arnold said.
Giesel called for narrowing the present trade imbalance between Mauritius and the United States.

"There is a very serious imbalance in U.S/Mauritius trade in favour of Mauritius. We are now giving Mauritius trade opportunities with the best and most advanced industries in the world," Giesel said.

In 1995, Mauritius exported some 4.0 billion rupees ($193 million) of goods to the United States, mostly textile products and raw sugar. Mauritian imports from the U.S. totalled 891 million rupees during the same year.
